translationRepairs: Wenshao laid out in detail how to aid Guizhou and guard the frontier, put military affairs in the hands of Surveillance Commissioner Xi Baotian, and directed subordinates such as Su Yuanchun and Gong Jichang in the campaign; the rebel leader Zhang Xiuhui was beheaded at Wuyapo, and Guizhou was pacified.

Wenshao laid out in detail how to aid Guizhou and guard the frontier, put military affairs in the hands of Surveillance Commissioner Xi Baotian, and directed subordinates such as Su Yuanchun and Gong Jichang in the campaign; the rebel leader Zhang Xiumei was beheaded at Wuyapo, and Guizhou was pacified.
s0046 names 張秀眉; 秀眉 is Xiumei, so Zhang Xiuhui is a misreading. The proposed idiomatic restores the correct name without other changes.

Wenshao itemized and submitted plans for aiding Guizhou and defending the borders; he entrusted military affairs to surveillance commissioner Xi Baotian, supervised his subordinate generals Su Yuanchun, Gong Jichang, and others in advance and suppression, beheaded the chief rebel Zhang Xiuhui at Wuyapo, and Guizhou was pacified.

Wenshao itemized and submitted plans for aiding Guizhou and defending the borders; he entrusted military affairs to surveillance commissioner Xi Baotian, supervised his subordinate generals Su Yuanchun, Gong Jichang, and others in advance and suppression, beheaded the chief rebel Zhang Xiumei at Wuyapo, and Guizhou was pacified.
The same 張秀眉 in s0046 must be Zhang Xiumei in the literal; Xiuhui invents a wrong reading of 眉, and the proposed wording fixes only that name.
He died that winter at seventy-nine; the court posthumously made him Grand Tutor and gave him the posthumous title Wenqin.
He died that winter at seventy-nine; the court posthumously made him Grand Guardian and gave him the posthumous title Wenqin.
s0092 reads 晉贈太保; 太保 is Grand Guardian, not 太傅 (Grand Tutor). The replacement restores the correct posthumous office.
That winter he died, aged seventy-nine; he was posthumously advanced to Grand Tutor and honored with the posthumous title Wenqin.
That winter he died, aged seventy-nine; he was posthumously advanced to Grand Guardian and honored with the posthumous title Wenqin.
s0092 likewise has 晉贈太保; rendering it Grand Tutor confuses 太保 with 太傅. Grand Guardian matches the Chinese title.
He was posthumously made Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Wenxiang.
He was posthumously made Grand Guardian and given the posthumous title Wenxiang.
s0191 is 贈太保; Grand Tutor is the wrong office (太傅). The proposed Grand Guardian wording matches the Chinese.
He was posthumously given Grand Tutor and honored with the posthumous title Wenxiang.
He was posthumously given Grand Guardian and honored with the posthumous title Wenxiang.
s0191 again reads 贈太保; the prior literal’s Grand Tutor is inaccurate, and Grand Guardian correctly renders 太保.
When a circuit intendant privately accepted two hundred thousand taels from a merchant as a birthday gift in exchange for mining rights at Haizhou, Zhidong impeached and dismissed him at once.
When a circuit intendant privately presented two hundred thousand taels of merchant money as a birthday gift and asked to open mines at Haizhou, Zhidong impeached and dismissed him at once.

s0178 is 私獻商人金二十萬為壽，請開礦海州: the intendant privately offered merchant money as a birthday gift and asked to open mines, not accepted a gift from a merchant. The proposed idiomatic restores agent direction and request.
A circuit intendant privately presented a merchant two hundred thousand taels as a birthday gift and asked to open mines at Haizhou; Zhidong immediately impeached and removed him.
A circuit intendant privately presented two hundred thousand taels of a merchant's gold as a birthday gift and asked to open mines at Haizhou; Zhidong immediately impeached and removed him.
私獻商人金 marks 商人金 as the gift object (merchant gold), not a merchant as recipient. The prior literal reverses the dative; the proposed wording fixes that.
